messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Stan and Intel MKL?
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering if we should tweak Stan such that it can specifically take advantage of the MKL? I know this thing cost money, but those who have it get some speedups here for free (assuming its there). Use cases

1. Enabling the MKL for Eigen gave me ~10-20% speedup. Depending on your model you may get even more.

2. It is possible to make CVODES use the Intel MKL. I have never tried this, but from talking to people this may give a 2X speedup for ODE solving; again "for free".

Specifically what I have in mind to do is to let the build system define a macro, called

STAN_USE_MKL

for example. If this macro is defined, then CVODES is instructed to be built slightly different and will then use MKL routines which hopefully expedite things.

Another advantage to deploy this in a pre-configured way is that we can ensure that the MKL is used in the right way as you can shoot yourself in the foot otherwise. At least the unit tests of stan-math are not successful whenever you switch on all optimizations from the Intel compiler.

Would that be an appropiate approach?

Sebastian

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan and Intel MKL?
parts:
Hi!

Yes, this is a good topic for the meetings. Let me clarify that two things are involved here:

- MKL
- Intel compiler

The MKL can come independent of the Intel compiler while the Intel compiler usually brings with it the MKL. As far as I am aware neither are free, only if you use it for academic only purposes there are some possibilities to use them free of charge.

I myself was always curious at what the real speedup for CVODES is - the 2X sounds to good to be true, but I am already happy with a 1.5X. The changes this implies, I can easily maintain; but I can't do magic, i.e. I can do so with what we have here which is the 2015.3 version (the second latest to my knowledge).

Wrt. to stan-math and the Intel compiler: You have to enable the options "-fp-model precise -fp-model source" in order to get units tests to pass (I am not sure if the cmdstan manual states this). As far as I recall, I did not dare to throw in the MKL on top of that, but I can investigate should we want this.

Best,
Sebastian

Let's go in steps here:

1. Ensure in the built system that the intel compiler is called with the right options

2. Include in the build system a flag for having the MKL which allows to instruct Eigen to use MKL as well

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan and Intel MKL?
parts:
Non-programmer here, but what isn't the MKL just a highly tuned BLAS/LAPACK combination? If Stan is already calling the local BLAS & LAPACK the speedup should happen.

Possibly the reason why you don't see as much is that Stan made the decision to use Eigen, which specifically does not use the system BLAS but for philosophical reasons builds its own routines. See these two messages by the authors of Armadillo (which uses BLAS/LAPACK) and RcppEigen on the R-devel list from 2012:

* http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/rcpp-devel/2012-June/003899.html
* http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/rcpp-devel/2012-June/003909.html

So in Stan's case, unless Eigen has greatly changed from 2012, the benefit of using the MKL (or OpenBLAS or ATLAS) will be restricted to the non-Eigen sections of the code, I believe.

Thanks,

Avi

Correct. Eigen replaces some of its calls with MKL optimized routines. The same holds true for CVODES if you compile it correctly.

In summary, we are talking about conditional builds which I have already done, will anyway maintain and are suggesting to add to Stan.

@Ben: Yes, wherever the MKL is around, the Intel compiler will be close and vice versa. However, from my experience with Stan and R I would NOT setup a production system to build with Intel anymore. If you make as a company the decision to go with open-soruce, then you should actually use the compilers of that community. This means the optimal system from my perspective is built on the Rtools compiler (gcc 4.9 as of now) and then you simply link in the MKL. That would have saved me (and other here, sorry) a lot of trouble.

> If we offer an option to build with Intel MKL and users
> try it and it doesn't work, they'll send us questions and we
> don't want to ignore users questions. In this case, we'd just
> direct them all to you. This is what happens with various
> R configs, MSVC compilers, edge-case g++ compilers on linux,
> etc.
>
> Then for this to be useful, there needs to be instructions on
> how to build for CmdStan, PyStan, RStan, etc.
>

> unit tests for the math lib, Stan, and interfaces pass as is?
>
> Or even worse, will the code need to be hacked to make it work?
>
> - Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan and Intel MKL?

Nobody's signing any contracts for support :-) I just meant
that if you don't do it, it's unlikely anyone else will, so we'd
just remove the feature.
